SOURCE: "Summer Camps & Programs" (1983). Internet Archive item summercampsprogr0000gold.
        Lending-restricted; CANNOT be read from here. Assembled 2026-09-06 from nine overlapping
        Open Library search-inside windows. A RECONSTRUCTION, not a transcription.

The book's own index carries "Kamp Kanawana-Montreal YMCA, 172-173", so the camp has a
TWO-PAGE entry. What follows is the head of that entry only. The rest of pages 172-173 —
the fee figures, the session dates, the facilities and whatever narrative the guide prints —
was recovered on a second, slower pass later the same day and is set out below. What is still
unread is whatever else fills two printed pages beyond the fields transcribed here.

QUERIES: "Kamp Kanawana" ; "Kanawana" "Boys and girls" Quebec ; "190 boys and girls, ages 7-19" ;
         "KAMP KANAWANA-MONTREAL YMCA Category General" ; "Summer Address Box 310, St. Sauveur" ;
         "St. Sauveur des Monts, Quebec, JOR 1RO Canada" ; "Summer Telephone (514) 227-2414" ;
         "Winter Address 1441 Drummond Street" ; "Quebec H3G 1W3 Canada Winter Telephone" ;
         "Winter Telephone (514) 849-5331 Director Louis Jean"

RECONSTRUCTED, as the fields run (the walk was resumed and finished later the same day):

  KAMP KANAWANA-MONTREAL YMCA
  Category      General
  Participants  190 boys and girls, ages 7-19
  Summer Address    Box 310, St. Sauveur des Monts, Quebec, JOR 1RO Canada
  Summer Telephone  (514) 227-2414
  Winter Address    1441 Drummond Street, Montreal, Quebec H3G 1W3 Canada
  Winter Telephone  (514) 849-5331
  Director      Louis Jean
  Sessions      Four 2-week from end of June to third week in August, depending on program
  Fees          Residential: $370 -- 2 weeks; Wilderness: $385 -- 2 weeks
  Facts         Located 50 miles north of Montreal on 1,000 acres of wooded property, this is a
                resident camp, with programs in wilderness tripping and counselor-training
                offered. Both French- and English-speaking children attend, although the program
                is conducted in English. [...]

ON THE DIRECTOR FIELD. Two windows straddle it -- "...1W3 Canada Winter Telephone (514) 849-5331
Director Louis Jean Sessions Four 2-week from end of June to..." and "...Telephone (514) 849-5331
Director Louis Jean Sessions Four 2-week from end of June to third week in August..." -- so the
field is EXACTLY TWO WORDS and runs straight into the next label. NO SURNAME WAS PRINTED. That
weakens the easiest reading, that a surname was lost to the scan: nothing was lost, because
nothing stood there. Either the compiler received "Louis Jean" as the whole name, or a surname
was dropped before printing. Note that this guide's Director fields elsewhere carry two-word
names of the same shape -- one nearby entry reads "Louis Simon" -- and that "Jean" is a real
Quebec surname. The name does not occur anywhere else in this project.
See conflict c_065 for how it sits against Peter Goddard, who signed a Kanawana newsletter as
"Director" on 15 November 1982.

ON THE FIGURES. 190 boys and girls, ages 7-19, continues the registered-capacity series this
project has from the national directories: 180 in 1975 (90 boys and 90 girls, 8-15) and 189 in
1976 (98 boys and 91 girls, 8-15). The age band has widened at both ends, from 8-15 to 7-19,
which is what an entry covering the CIT and LIT programmes alongside the camp would look like.
The addresses and both telephone numbers match those printed in the 1975 and 1976 national
directories.
